name: MoEQuant: Enhancing Quantization for Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models via Expert-Balanced Sampling and Affinity Guidance
problem: PTQ degrades MoE models far worse than dense models, and the usual dense calibration set starves rarely-activated experts.
mechanism: Names two MoE-specific calibration pathologies and fixes both: (1) INTER-EXPERT IMBALANCE - token routing is uneven, so a random calibration set under-samples and biases rarely-used experts, fixed by Expert-Balanced Self-Sampling (EBSS) which constructs a calibration set whose per-expert sample counts match expected routing frequency; (2) INTRA-EXPERT IMBALANCE - the weighted aggregation of a token's experts makes the effective per-expert signal differ from the raw activations, fixed by Affinity Guidance which scores calibration samples by how strongly they align with their assigned expert.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): PTQ on MoE suffers severe accuracy degradation and diminished generalization, and MoEQuant is a quantization framework tailored for MoE LLMs addressing both imbalances. The abstract gives NO numeric accuracy delta or throughput figure, so speedup_reported stays descriptive. The transferable contribution is the diagnosis: MoE PTQ fails on calibration coverage, not on weight bit width.
